name: otr-many-facts
about: An over-the-road job with many facts: enough for five angles that differ in kind.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: Family owned, and the owner still drives

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook equipment_first (equipment first) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $402.10 in the last 28 days over 30100 impressions and brought 14 leads, $28.72 per lead.

output.audience: Experienced Class A over-the-road drivers who meet the experience requirement and will run reefer across the full operating area. They hold an OTR seat now. The pay per mile, a newer truck and a pet in the cab would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the newer truck itself, parked and clean, and name it as a reefer seat.
angles.proof: The job lists newer trucks and reefer equipment.
angles.why: This hook and scene is the only combination measured, and its cost per lead sits under the benchmark pause line. The lead count is modest, so treat it as a lean, not proof.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile in plain type, with health insurance, retirement plan and paid time off beneath it.
angles.proof: The job states the pay per mile and offers health insurance, a retirement plan and paid time off.
angles.why: Pay is the fact an OTR driver compares most readily, and a plain background keeps it readable. No pay-led ad has been measured here yet.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A, the stated experience, reefer, all the states the job covers, the stated weeks.
angles.proof: The job states the licence class, a years figure, a weeks figure and the states covered.
angles.why: Stating requirements filters out drivers who cannot qualify. The years and weeks items are unlabelled on the sheet, so the office should confirm what each means before writing.

angles.idea: Lead with life in the cab: a pet riding along on a long run, with the job's freight-handling detail beneath.
angles.proof: The job allows pets, and its freight-handling detail is on the sheet for the writer to use as written.
angles.why: Long-haul work is easier with company in the cab, and the view from the cab can show that. Nothing has been measured on this hook.

angles.idea: Lead with the carrier's own words: family owned, and the owner still drives.
angles.proof: The job's own description says the carrier is family owned and the owner still drives.
angles.why: An owner who drives is a claim a driver can check, and it sets this carrier apart. It reuses the scene that has brought leads, with a hook that has not been measured.
